newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spot end down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spot end down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Tuesday on a technical correction after Monday's sharp rises, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell slightly to 16.71 percent from 17.00 percent.
Total turnover shrank to 8.83 million lots from 10.77 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

But the three-day contract bucked the trend and rose to 28.00 percent from 20.00 percent due to surging short-term fund demand today and tomorrow for new domestic A share issues and listings on both Shanghai and Shenzhen bourses, traders said.
Traders expected the three-day and seven-day contracts to go up in the next few trading days due to the increasing fund demand trigged by the new share issues and listings.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down with the three-year contract most affected by the issue of the new two-year treasury note, which will start tomorrow.
The weighted average price of the two-year discount T-note has been set at 82.39 yuan, with a return rate of over 10 percent, higher than the market had expected, traders said.
"The higher-than-expected returns have led to institutional selling in the existing contracts today," said one trader.
The most active three-year note that matures in Sept 1999 lost to 102.36 yuan today from 102.60 yuan on Monday.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 811,639 lots from 1.16 million lots.
Traders said market sentiment was weakened by expected hot sales of the new two-year bond and prices were likely to go down in the short term.
In addition, a fund shortfall before the Chinese Lunar New Year in early February would also prevent the contracts from rising, traders said.
